original_query: select  i_item_id,         s_state, grouping(s_state) g_state,         avg(ss_quantity) agg1,         avg(ss_list_price) agg2,         avg(ss_coupon_amt) agg3,         avg(ss_sales_price) agg4 from store_sales, customer_demographics, date_dim, store, item where ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and       ss_item_sk = i_item_sk and       ss_store_sk = s_store_sk and       ss_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk and       cd_gender = 'M' and       cd_marital_status = 'S' and       cd_education_status = 'College' and       d_year = 2002 and       s_state = 'IL' and      i_category  = 'Jewelry'  group by rollup (i_item_id, s_state)  order by i_item_id          ,s_state  limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH filtered_sales AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id,
           ss.ss_quantity,
           ss.ss_list_price,
           ss.ss_coupon_amt,
           ss.ss_sales_price
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN store s ON ss.ss_store_sk = s.s_store_sk
    JOIN item i ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN customer_demographics cd ON ss.ss_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2002
      AND s.s_state = 'IL'
      AND i.i_category = 'Jewelry'
      AND cd.cd_gender = 'M'
      AND cd.cd_marital_status = 'S'
      AND cd.cd_education_status = 'College'
),
item_agg AS (
    SELECT i_item_id,
           AVG(ss_quantity) AS agg1,
           AVG(ss_list_price) AS agg2,
           AVG(ss_coupon_amt) AS agg3,
           AVG(ss_sales_price) AS agg4
    FROM filtered_sales
    GROUP BY i_item_id
),
grand_agg AS (
    SELECT AVG(ss_quantity) AS agg1,
           AVG(ss_list_price) AS agg2,
           AVG(ss_coupon_amt) AS agg3,
           AVG(ss_sales_price) AS agg4
    FROM filtered_sales
)
SELECT i_item_id,
       'IL'::bpchar AS s_state,
       0 AS g_state,
       agg1, agg2, agg3, agg4
FROM item_agg
UNION ALL
SELECT i_item_id,
       NULL::bpchar AS s_state,
       1 AS g_state,
       agg1, agg2, agg3, agg4
FROM item_agg
UNION ALL
SELECT NULL::bpchar AS i_item_id,
       NULL::bpchar AS s_state,
       1 AS g_state,
       agg1, agg2, agg3, agg4
FROM grand_agg
ORDER BY i_item_id, s_state
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Since s_state is constrained to a constant ('IL') by the WHERE clause, the ROLLUP(i_item_id, s_state) contains a redundant grouping dimension: the (i_item_id, s_state) grouping set and the (i_item_id) grouping set produce identical aggregates. The rollup can be replaced with GROUPING SETS ((i_item_id), ()) and the item-level rows duplicated via UNION ALL, reducing grouping-set work.

Replace the implicit comma join with explicit JOIN ... ON syntax for readability; the optimizer already pushes all single-table equality filters, so moving predicates into ON clauses yields no performance change.

The execution plan already uses index scans (date_dim, store_sales via idx_store_sales_date_store, item and customer_demographics primary-key probes) with a nested-loop join; no further join-order rewrite is beneficial without additional indexes on store_sales(ss_item_sk).
